title: Personal offline instruction graphlet design notes
body:
Quick brain-dump / proto-level sketch for an offline-first instruction execution primitive: 'graphlets'.

Goal
- Allow client devices (mobile, offline desktops, edge nodes) to capture, execute, and later reconcile small units of instruction/interaction (graphlets) with Redwood's runtime.
- Preserve auditability and deterministic replayability for scoring, billing, and regression detection.

Motivation / use-cases- intermittent connectivity: collect user interactions locally, pre-run local heuristics, then batch-stitch into server-side session for final outputs or audit.
- privacy-first: run private transforms and redact before upload.
- latency-sensitive features: pre-warm expected next-instruction paths.

Constraints / non-goals- Not trying to move full model execution offline. Focus is on instruction fragments, metadata, and small inference-friendly pre-steps.
- Keep on-device footprint small (metadata-first, optional small tokenized prefixes only).

High-level idea- Represent each user interaction or micro-instruction as a graphlet: a compact manifest + optional compacted tokens + small local verdicts.
- Graphlets have typed edges (parent->child, suggestion->accept, rerank->winner, toolcall->response_ref).
- Server accepts graphlets and runs a stitcher that validates ordering, resolves conflicts, and optionally re-executes final model call if needed.

Graphlet manifest (human sketch)- id: stable opaque id (uuidv4)
- created_ts: iso8601
- client_id: client device id (hashed)
- session_hint: optional server session id or tag
- parent_ids: []
- kind: {prompt_fragment, prewarm_probe, rerank_hint, tool_call_stub, moderation_probe}
- compact_tokens: base64(CDSv0) or null (CDSv0 = compact delta serialization, see below)
- local_signals: map string->string (entropy_bucket, intent_score, sampling_seed) // serialize as kv list
- privacy_mask: {redaction_blob_ref | inline_redacted_text} // optional
- deterministic_nonce: 64-bit hex (for dedupe)
- client_signature: ed25519(sig over manifest+compact_tokens)
- schema_version: "graphlet.v1"

Compact Delta Serialization (CDSv0) - idea
- tokenized prefix deltas relative to last acknowledged server cursor. Format is intentionally tiny: run-length plus short token diffs. Encoded as base64 to avoid nested payloads in manifest. Example: "RLE:5|+12,34,-7|len:18" (documented separately).

Server-side stitcher responsibilities
- validate signatures and deterministic_nonce to dedupe repeated uploads.
- assemble graphlet DAGs per session_hint and time window.
- detect forks: if client did two conflicting edits, mark both and surface to conflict-resolution policy.
- run replay check: if compact_tokens present, optionally perform tokenized replay to assert same tokenization and length expectations.
- transform local_signals into server telemetry buckets.
- if graphlet.kind indicates rerank_hint or tool_call_stub, the stitcher may enqueue a re-execution with canonical prompt.

API shape (sketch for client->server endpoint)
POST /v1/graphlets/batchUpload  Content-Type: application/json
Request body (example as text):
[
  {
    "id": "uuid-1111",
    "created_ts": "2026-02-18T16:14:21Z",
    "client_id": "dev-83a6...",
    "session_hint": "sess-4f12",
    "parent_ids": ["uuid-1099"],
    "kind": "prompt_fragment",
    "compact_tokens": "<base64-cds>",
    "local_signals": ["entropy_bucket=3","prefetch=high"],
    "privacy_mask": "redacted:v1:sha256:...",
    "deterministic_nonce": "0x12ab...",
    "client_signature": "base64sig...",
    "schema_version": "graphlet.v1"
  }
]

Server response (text sketch)
{
  "uploaded": ["uuid-1111"],
  "dupes": [],
  "errors": []
}

Design considerations- determinism: clients must derive deterministic_nonce from stable inputs to avoid accidental duplicates when retrying uploads.
- attestations: client_signature lets server decide if the graphlet is trusted or needs additional verification. Edge devices without HSM can still sign with ephemeral keys; trust tier added in metadata.
- cost accounting: price a graphlet ingest (lightweight) vs stitch-time re-exec (heavy). Track per-graphlet flags that trigger re-exec to estimate downstream cost.
- privacy: if privacy_mask present, server must not attempt to reconstruct redacted text; privacy_mask should be verifiable (hashes) so client can't claim redaction but upload plaintext.

On-device behaviors (sketch)- capture a graphlet when: user stops typing for 300ms OR tool call stub created OR model prewarm probe triggered.
- persist graphlets in circular buffer (N=4096 or size cap), evict oldest fully-acked by server.
- background uploader runs exponential backoff with batched uploads grouped by session_hint.

Conflict resolution heuristics (server side)- timestamp precedence with nonce tie-breaker.
- when non-deterministic merges required, create a 'merge-probe' graphlet that includes both branches and an instruction to rerank; surface to product team for UX.

Edge cases- device time drift: server primarily uses created_ts but will accept reported client_ts if within 48h of server ingest; otherwise mark as skewed.
- offline edits diverging from server: if replay mismatch on compact_tokens, mark graphlet as mismatch and optionally run full re-execution.

Telemetry and observability- log ingestion latency, dedupe rate, re-exec ratio, per-client upload success.
- add a lightweight per-graphlet 'cost_tag' indicating expected stitch CPU/tokens to help with billing sampling.

Security & keys- rollout plan: start with software keys for alpha devices, require HSM for enterprise clients.
- key rotation: clients must support remote key rotation and ephemeral signing windows.

Open questions / TODOs
- formalize CDSv0 spec (RLE, diffs, escape rules).
- decide canonical client_id hashing strategy to preserve anonymity while enabling device-level heuristics.
- UX: how to expose merged conflicts to user without spamming.
- telemetry quotas: avoid clients generating excessive tiny graphlets (rate limit at client and server).

Next steps for prototype- implement minimal SDK: client capture + batch upload + deterministic_nonce generator (1 week).
- lightweight server stub to validate signatures, store manifests, run simple DAG assembly and return ack.
- small simulation harness to replay 10k synthetic graphlets and measure dedupe/mismatch rates.

Notes to self- keep schema flat and string-first to make it friendly for mobile storage (prefer JSON arrays of strings).
- avoid embedding large token arrays inline; use compact binary blobs referenced by base64 id.

End of scratchpad.
